contract: F-11, the updates/update.log unlock line (T3.10; W-14, CF-23, F-10): after every unlock attempt, a success and every refusal, the app appends one `r1-app <os> unlock ...` line. It is the only durable trace of a refused unlock: the app log and the audit events of a session spent at the lock screen end with it (docs/app-updates.md 8.2). The frame, the time and the token rules V, I, E, C and the sentinels are vectors.json's; this file adds the unlock event, its two new token rules (N, A) and its vectors

tokens.N: a signed integer: -?[0-9]{1,10} (the shape of SQLite's user_version, a signed 32-bit number); the numeric shape only, never a word rule
tokens.A: the stamp's applied-through token: [0-9A-Za-z._-]{1,16}. Word-shaped and data-fed (the second field of the workspace file's last_writer stamp, which another build wrote): release 1 writes `interim`, P10 (T10.3) defines the later values; a longer or other-shaped token is omitted, never an error. Only `applied` names it
tokens.registered: unlock (T3.10) joins startup and start-failed in UPDATE_LOG_EVENTS, as data: its keys in a fixed order, each with one rule (a token rule with the sentinels it admits, or a closed list)

rules.result: closed: ok, wrong_password, vault_damaged, workspace_schema_unreadable, vault_open_failed, vault_missing, vault_descriptor_missing, vault_descriptor_unreadable, vault_recovery_blocked, workspace_newer, error. `ok` or the answer's reason; anything else is `error`
rules.user_version: N, data-fed: the workspace file's own user_version before the migrations (the decrypted file's SQLite header, read only when its first 16 bytes are SQLite's magic), or a newer database's found; omitted when there is none
rules.writer: V with the sentinels `none` and `unreadable`, data-fed: the last_writer stamp the open found before its overwrite, through parseLastWriter (F-10). `none`: no stamp (no schema_meta, no row, a value that is not text); `unreadable`: parseLastWriter says so, or its version fails V. Omitted when the open never got as far as the stamp: `writer` omitted and `writer=none` mean different things
rules.applied: A, data-fed: the stamp's second field, only beside a `writer` that is a version; omitted when it fails A
rules.what: closed: database, descriptor, kdf, frame, journal: which version `found` is (workspace_newer)
rules.found: I, data-fed: the version a newer build wrote, only when it is an integer of the I rule (a vault format's found may be a string cut from the file: omitted unless its text passes I)
rules.err: E: a refusal's or a failure's error code; a SQLite result code as SQLITE_<n> (an integer errcode 0-65535 wins over ERR_SQLITE_ERROR, start-failure.ts's rule); never a message
rules.syscall: C: the bare system call of what the `error` arm caught

fields.why_per_result: The fields are chosen per result, so fields that cannot occur together never share a line: all nine keys at their caps would exceed the 256-byte frame, and each result's longest line fits it (u61 is the longest of all). vault_open_failed carries no syscall (the open's failures are SQLite errors); vault_missing carries no keptCopyDiscarded (a later version may add a key: readers ignore keys they do not know). No line at all for an unlock of a workspace already open (nothing was checked) or a password that is not a string (a malformed call, which costs no key derivation)

emit.how: `line` is the exact line the HEAD writer emits for the input (platform and time are inputs). `open` is what the unlock's open handed out: null when nothing was decrypted; `user_version` the header's (null: not read, or no SQLite magic); `previous` the raw last_writer value the open found before its overwrite (null: none), absent when the open never got as far as the stamp (the vault parses it, so the raw value never leaves it). `thrown` is what the attempt threw, as the class and its constructor arguments, or an Error with own properties (`props`) and getters that throw (`throwing_getters`); null for a success. `never`: texts that must not appear
